column2: Recommended Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule for Ages 18 Years or Younger
column4: 2025 (revised 07/02/2025). CDC does not endorse this application or its use of the material. The material is available free of charge on the CDC website at https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/hcp/imz-schedules/child-adolescent-age.html. This transcription is simplified for display (one line per antigen and dose; risk-group and catch-up rules are left out) and must not be read as CDC's own text; every age and series is kept as CDC states it. Trade names are CDC's: “The use of trade names is for identification purposes only and does not imply endorsement by the ACIP or CDC.”

(verify) end of window derived: CDC prints no end age for this dose; 8 months is where the second-season bar “1 dose (8 through 19 months)” starts. Nirsevimab, a monoclonal antibody: “1 dose depending on maternal RSV vaccination status”. Born October–March: “administer 1 dose nirsevimab within 1 week of birth”; born April–September: “shortly before start of RSV season”; “Mother received RSV vaccine at least 14 days prior to delivery: nirsevimab not needed”.

High-risk groups only: “1 dose (8 through 19 months), See Notes”: chronic lung disease of prematurity, severe immunocompromise, cystic fibrosis with severity criteria, or American Indian or Alaska Native: “1 dose nirsevimab shortly before start of second RSV season”.

CDC: “Birth”. “Birth weight ≥2,000 grams: 1 dose within 24 hours of birth if medically stable”; “Birth weight <2,000 grams: 1 dose at chronological age 1 month or hospital discharge”. Monovalent HepB only.
